title: Updating the Private Key for GCP

blocks.text: The private key is a confidential string associated with a GCP service account, which is necessary to access the service account from outside the Google Cloud environment, such as on other platforms or on-premises infrastructure. During the GCP account onboarding process, a private key is generated in JSON format when you apply the tree discovery template, which is then provided to DSPM as part of the account onboarding process.
If your service account keys need to be updated or have expired, you can update your service account key at any time.
You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with permission to add accounts in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Download a private key for your service account in JSON format from the Google Cloud Console. To learn more on downloading a private key for a service account, refer to the Google Cloud documentation.
To update the private key, on the Zscaler Admin Console:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Cloud Accounts.
On the Cloud Accounts page, select the GCP account for which you want to update the private key.
Click Manage, and then select Update Private Key from the drop-down menu.

In the Update Private Key window, upload the downloaded JSON file to the Zscaler Admin Console by either dragging and dropping the file, or clicking or click to browse to select the file from your computer.
DSPM validates the updated private key by verifying it against the service account. If the validation is successful, a message appears indicating that the connection is established.
If the private key is invalid, or it does not match the service account, an error is displayed.

blocks.text: The private key is updated for the selected service account.
